question:
RECOMMEND: APPROVE — merge.

Why: 20 of 20 acceptance criteria evidenced, verdict PASSED, and the two interactive criteria were closed by your own drive of the deployed staging app rather than by any harness. Staging was restored byte-identical to its pre-import snapshot and production was never touched at any point. Every claim in the build report was independently reproduced by a fresh agent, including re-running the falsification harness against the real source.

DECISION EFFECT — this one is unusual, so read it before approving:

Approving does NOT import anything into your live app. This branch ships NO deployable code — nothing under app/ or functions/src/. I verified that independently. What merges is tooling: an extractor, an importer, their tests, and a --target flag. Your production data is identical the moment after merge as the moment before.

The actual production import is a SEPARATE deliberate act, later, that you run and that refuses without its own APPROVED marker on a production normalization sheet. So this gate asks "is the tooling sound and proven", not "do I want my 2023-2024 data in the app". You decide the second question separately, whenever you like, and you will get manual-test steps for it then.

Rejecting sends it back to build with your feedback.

TWO THINGS TO SEE BEFORE SAYING YES:

(1) The merge/deploy shape is different here. Your README's `done` stage requires deploying to production and confirming it live. There is nothing to deploy — no app code changed — so that step is a no-op, and I will not run a firebase deploy to satisfy a ritual. I will say so plainly at the terminal boundary rather than quietly skipping it.

(2) Finding 2 needs a decision and is NOT part of this feature: History's "Paid by" filter matches nothing for ANY row in your app today, imported or not. It predates this work. I have not folded it in. It deserves its own entity if it bothers you.

artifacts.summary:
VERDICT: PASSED, 20 of 20. Checklist 3 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed. `status --read 061 --stage verify --ac-scan` reads EVERY criterion as evidenced — AC-19 with 4 citations, AC-2 with 3, AC-7 with 3, none unevidenced.

LIVE EVIDENCE — the stage's own requirement, satisfied twice over. The captain's drive of the deployed staging app at expense-sheet-staging.web.app on 2026-09-02: "2023 and 2024 both look right, all steps passed." Plus the verifier's own live runs against staging throughout. Notably her 2024 pass INCLUDES seeing December empty and not reporting it — the false-alarm case step 8 was rewritten to prevent after Finding 4.

REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY by a fresh agent, not read from the build report:
- Full suite re-run from scratch: 260 pass, 0 fail.
- Six defects reintroduced into the REAL shipped source one at a time, suite watched go red each time, files restored. Removing AC-19's residue assertion reddens exactly 1 test, proving nothing else in the suite can see a dropped column. Restoring the old label discriminator reddens 36.
- Live staging rehearsal end to end before the captain's drive: snapshot 1,405, apply 1,670, undo, hand-added row survived, byte-identical restore.
- Production re-read directly rather than trusted.

THE APPLY SHE DROVE ON:
    staging before 1,408 rows / 0 exp-hist-   ->   after 3,078 rows / 1,670 exp-hist-
    by year  2023: 895 | 2024: 775 | 2025: 1,403 | 2026: 5
    paid_by = ijac on all 1,670, resolved through the app's own USERS table
    Categories 28 before and after — none created
    both receipt digests matched at read AND at apply, so her approval bound to the exact bytes she reviewed

THE RESTORE, demonstrated with the same shipped function AC-1 uses:
    snapshot 1,408 == staging now 1,408, exp-hist- remaining 0
    modified 0, deleted 0, added 0  =>  BYTE-IDENTICAL
    Her step-9 add and step-11 delete net to zero, checked rather than assumed.

PRODUCTION at close: 2,168 rows, 0 exp-hist-, 25 Categories, tabs Expenses|Categories|Subscriptions|Users|SchedulerLog, no Migration tab, dates 2025/2026 only. Untouched throughout.

SURFACE: 10 files, +4,797 / -3. No deployable code — nothing under app/ or functions/src/.

REVIEWER FINDINGS, under this workflow's labels:

Needs decision:
- Finding 2 — History's `Paid by` filter matches nothing for any row in the app today, imported or not. Pre-existing, outside this feature's scope.

Deferred risk:
- Finding 1 — the archive workbook id is in source in a public repository; already on main from 060, so this branch does not introduce it.
- Finding 5 — an unmapped taxonomy pair would land in `Other` silently; 17 of 17 pairs map today and `Other` takes 4 of 1,670 rows. Promotes if the workbook grows an eighteenth pair.
- Finding 7 — AC-19's accounting window excludes the label and date-header rows, so the criterion whose job is catching silent drops is blind to one class of them. All three label rows verified clean today.
- Finding 8 — nothing in this feature DIAGNOSES a variance, only detects one; the entity filled that vacuum with a guess that survived three reviews.

Polish:
- Finding 4 — the 2024 record ends 2024-11-08 and nothing in this entity had recorded it. Not a defect. It changed the manual-test step that would otherwise have walked the captain into a false alarm.

Not material, routed for decision:
- Finding 6 — her "should be" figures come from row 32, whose per-row cells are FORMULAS, and the ranges in those formulas are wrong. September reaches into October 1st; October omits the 31st and adds November's entire month-total column; December drops the 31st. Her row-32 value equals her own formula's range exactly, and that range minus its extras plus its omissions equals our day-cell sum to 0.0000% in all three months. The extraction is exact and strictly MORE complete than her totals row — we read six day columns her formulas omit entirely, including the 2024 leap day.

Finding 3 — both environments drifted during the stage from the app's own scheduler, not from this work.

DELIVERY CAN PROCEED. No Material finding, no defect found in the extraction at any point, and the one investigation that looked like a defect resolved to a fault in the source spreadsheet rather than in the code.
